title: Transgenerational immune priming (TGIP) and its potential association with EGR1 in Penaeusvannamei.
reason: Penaeus vannamei primed with UV-inactivated Vibrio parahaemolyticus (inactivated pathogen, criterion 2), followed by bacterial challenge of primed F0 and of F1 offspring with survival, bacterial-load and immune outcomes (criterion 3); a primary peer-reviewed experiment, matching Lin_2025, Lv_2025 and BermeoCapunong_2026

title: Parental immune priming reshapes offspring growth, metabolism, and thermal tolerance in the Pacific Oyster
reason: Meets criteria 1-4 (poly(I:C) broodstock priming of Crassostrea gigas, then offspring growth and acute thermal challenge to 236 dpf), but it is a bioRxiv preprint - hold until a peer-reviewed version appears

title: Conserved transcriptomic heat stress response signatures in coral recruits selectively bred from thermally distinct broodstock in a low-differentiation system
reason: Selective breeding (warm x cool reef crosses) with a single heat-stress exposure of recruits; parental provenance is genetic, not an applied priming exposure, so criterion 2 fails (as for the selective-breeding coral precedents). Preprint, but excluded on merits rather than held.

title: Combined-stress priming alters physiology, transcriptional dynamics, and acute thermal resistance in Acropora cervicornis corals
reason: Acropora cervicornis primed 8 d with +3 C and/or +6 uM ammonium, 8 d recovery, then acute 15 h thermal challenge vs naive corals; meets criteria 1-4 but is a bioRxiv preprint - hold until peer-reviewed version appears

title: Sex-specific gut microbiota dysbiosis and intergenerational effects of florfenicol in Tigriopus japonicus: Maternal-only or biparental contributions?
reason: Marine copepod with chronic F0 florfenicol (pollutant/antibiotic) exposure and cross-mating to assess unexposed F1 development and sex ratio; meets criteria 1-4, analogous to the included Tigriopus japonicus pollutant transgenerational rows (Zhao_2024, Lee_2023)

title: MicroRNA-mediated transgenerational plasticity reveals pathways for ocean warming resilience
reason: Coral reef fish (Acanthochromis polyacanthus) - excluded by inclusion criterion 1; preprint status moot since it would not otherwise qualify

title: Thermal history modulates PFUnDA and PFTeDA toxicity in the Mediterranean mussel Mytilus galloprovincialis.
reason: Mytilus galloprovincialis given a 6 d sublethal thermal pre-exposure (23 C), then a later 14 d PFAS challenge at 17 C compared with non-pre-exposed mussels; priming-then-challenge design meets criteria 2 and 3 (thermal priming, so bivalve_temp_ph cluster despite the pollutant challenge)

title: From Bad to Worse: Carryover Effects Alter Responses to Multiple Stressors
reason: Mytilus edulis nanoplastic pre-exposure followed by later copper, nutrient and salinity stressors with survival and metabolic outcomes; meets criteria 1-4 (pollutant carryover, cf. Lee_2023 and SolDourdin_2024), but it is a bioRxiv preprint, so held until a peer-reviewed version appears

title: Feeding behaviour of broodstock Penaeus monodon fed live and frozen polychaetes
reason: Penaeus monodon broodstock feeding-behaviour trial comparing live vs frozen polychaete diets; a diet comparison is not a sublethal priming exposure (fails criterion 2), so the missing abstract does not leave inclusion genuinely open

title: Early life trade-offs in corals selected for adult heat tolerance are absent under heat stress
reason: Selective breeding from parents ranked by heat tolerance (genetic selection), not a sublethal priming exposure; the parental heatwave assay was a tolerance phenotyping step rather than conditioning, so criterion 2 fails (cf. 'Predicting selection-response gradients of heat tolerance'). Preprint status is moot because the paper is excluded.

title: High relatedness in sexually produced restoration cohorts of the endangered elkhorn coral, Acropora palmata
reason: No priming exposure (criterion 2): population-genetic assessment of relatedness and diversity in assisted-sexual-reproduction restoration cohorts of Acropora palmata, with no sublethal pre-exposure or later challenge; preprint status moot since it would be excluded anyway

title: Benefit or burden? Effects of repeated heat exposure on thermal tolerance, energetics, and immunity in the blue mussel Mytilus edulis.
reason: Baltic Mytilus repeated heat stress (4 cycles of 2.5 h at 27 C) then 4 d recovery, followed by an acute warming cardiac assay and a prolonged 27 C 5 d challenge versus naive mussels; all four criteria met (outcome Worsened, 100% mortality in primed group, as in Georgoulis_2021-style hardening design)

title: Predicting Coral Offspring Survival From Reef Thermal Histories in Ningaloo World Heritage Reef.
reason: No conditioning phase (criterion 2): selectively bred Acropora larvae given a single acute heat assay, with survival modelled against parental reef thermal history from satellite SST; this is a heritable-tolerance/provenance correlation with no applied priming exposure or common-garden conditioning contrast (cf. the selection-response gradients exclusion)

title: Predicting Coral Offspring Survival From Reef Thermal Histories in Ningaloo World Heritage Reef
reason: No conditioning phase (criterion 2): larvae from selectively bred Acropora families given a single acute heat assay, with survival modelled against parental-reef satellite SST history; the provenance is a correlate of genetic/historical thermal regime, not a deliberate or demonstrable priming exposure carried into a common garden followed by a later challenge.

title: Extended genomic regions flanking ultraconserved elements allow efficient species identification and intraspecific diversity assessment in coral
reason: Coral genomic methods paper (UCE-based species identification using existing data); no priming exposure or later outcome and not a primary conditioning experiment (fails criteria 2-4); preprint status moot since it would be excluded anyway

title: Autogenous vaccination protects Pacific oysters against OsHV-1 by reshaping the transcriptome.
reason: Magallana gigas primed with heat-treated or sublethal live OsHV-1 (at 18 C or 22 C) before a virulent OsHV-1 challenge at 22 C, with survival (RPS 57.5-85.0%), viral load and transcriptome outcomes; meets all four criteria (cf. de_Kantzow_2023b).

title: Optimization of immune priming interval using Imuno-FS Plus enhances the efficacy of oral formalin-killed Vibrio parahaemolyticus vaccine in Pacific white shrimp (Litopenaeus vannamei)
reason: Penaeus (Litopenaeus) vannamei given an oral formalin-killed Vibrio parahaemolyticus vaccine, then a live virulent V. parahaemolyticus challenge with survival/RPS scored, which meets criteria 2-3 as with BermeoCapunong_2026. The Imuno-FS Plus feed adjuvant does not count as priming by itself; the inactivated-pathogen vaccine does.

title: CgSMARCC2 modulates chromatin accessibility to regulate haemocyte proliferation in the immune priming of oyster Crassostrea gigas.
reason: Crassostrea gigas primed with Vibrio splendidus, then given a secondary V. splendidus stimulation; chromatin state was assessed 7 d after the first stimulation, and gene expression and haemocyte proliferation after the second. Same priming-then-secondary-stimulation design as the included Lian_2024, Lian_2025 and Sun_2025, so criteria 2 and 3 are met despite the RNAi mechanistic focus.

title: Effects of replacing fishmeal with Antarctic krill meal on growth and reproductive performance of Litopenaeus vannamei broodstock
reason: Dietary fishmeal replacement (feed formulation) trial on shrimp broodstock growth and reproduction, not a sublethal priming exposure followed by a later challenge (fails criterion 2); preprint status moot since it would not otherwise be included

title: Pathogen priming reveals host immune training and microbiome conditioning in corals
reason: Coral primed with non-lethal live or inactivated Vibrio coralliilyticus then challenged with subsequent infection under heat stress meets criteria 1-4, but it is a bioRxiv preprint; held until a peer-reviewed version appears

title: The Priming Impacts of Early Hypoxia Exposure in Abalone Parents Are Transmitted to Offspring.
reason: Haliotis discus hannai (gastropod) embryonic hypoxia exposure of F0 with F1 growth and hypoxia tolerance assessed years later; all four criteria met (extends Shen_2022 system to an intergenerational design)

title: Oral immune priming modulates microbiota composition and supports pathogen control in the Manila clam ( Ruditapes philippinarum )
reason: Meets all four criteria (sublethal live Vibrio europaeus oral priming of Ruditapes philippinarum followed by lethal secondary challenge, 87% vs 0% survival), but it is a bioRxiv preprint - hold until a peer-reviewed version appears

title: Shrimp endogenous viral elements (EVE) correlate with survival in white spot syndrome virus (WSSV) challenges
reason: No deliberate priming exposure (criterion 2): inherited endogenous viral elements are a genetic/breeding contrast, not a PAMP, inactivated-pathogen or sublethal-pathogen pre-exposure; offspring were naive before the WSSV challenge (also a bioRxiv preprint, but excluded on criterion 2 rather than held)

title: Maternal Large Yellow Tea Supplementation Confers Intergenerational Protection Against BPA-Induced Metabolic and Behavioral Disorders in Mice.
reason: Mouse study (terrestrial vertebrate) - fails inclusion criterion 1; the maternal intervention is also a dietary supplement, not a sublethal priming exposure

title: Developmental and transgenerational effects of climate change on inorganic mercury toxicity in a marine copepod.
reason: Marine copepod (Tigriopus japonicus) multigenerational F1-F4 design contrasting persistent (parental + offspring) vs offspring-only OA/OW/AW exposure, with later IHg toxicity and F4 transcriptome assessed; parental-history contrast satisfies criteria 2 and 3, matching the Zhao_2024 and Lee_2023 Tigriopus precedents

title: Addressing a Flat-Out Problem: Environmental DNA (eDNA) Exposes Silent Infestations of Acropora-Eating Flatworms (Prosthiostomum acroporae) in Coral Aquaculture.
reason: Methods paper developing a ddPCR eDNA assay for a coral pest flatworm; no sublethal priming exposure and no later-life or offspring outcome (fails criteria 2 and 3, and is methods-only under criterion 4)

title: Hatchery lobster releases risk genetic bottlenecking via survival skews with maternal effects
reason: European lobster hatchery parentage/genetic-diversity study; maternal effects arise from maternal size and identity, not a deliberate sublethal priming exposure or natural stress contrast (fails criterion 2)

title: Immune priming reshapes the microbiota and modulates pathogen dynamics in the Manila clam (Ruditapes philippinarum).
reason: Ruditapes philippinarum orally primed with sublethal live Vibrio europaeus then given a lethal secondary challenge (87% vs 0% survival); all four criteria hold, matching Li_2025a/Li_2025b sublethal-Vibrio priming precedents

title: Lead exposure modulates thermal vulnerability in Mytilus edulis under multi-stressor conditions.
reason: Mytilus edulis pre-exposed to sublethal Pb, then sequentially challenged with salinity and aerial heat stress; survival and transcriptome show cross-tolerance (criteria 2 and 3 met via priming-then-challenge design); pollutant priming falls in 'other'

title: Dietary phosphatidylinositol promotes ovarian maturation in Pacific white shrimp (Penaeus vannamei) via altered lipid mobilization and hormonal regulation.
reason: Dietary phospholipid supplementation (feed additive) with ovarian maturation measured during the 28 d feeding trial; not a sublethal priming exposure and no later-life or offspring assessment (fails criteria 2 and 3)

title: Pesticides commonly used in aquaculture: Interactive and repetitive effect of azamethiphos and deltamethrin on the physiology and growth of the mollusc Mytilus chilensis.
reason: Bivalve (Mytilus chilensis) pesticide study, but a repeated/chronic pulsed exposure with physiology and growth measured across and at the end of the exposure regime; no discrete priming phase followed by a later challenge or offspring assessment (fails criteria 2 and 3)

title: Multigenerational Exposure to Mancozeb Impacts Fitness Traits and Population Dynamics in Ceriodaphnia cornuta (Crustacea: Cladocera).
reason: Freshwater cladoceran (Ceriodaphnia cornuta) - fails the marine/estuarine inclusion criterion 1 (otherwise a multigenerational fungicide exposure with a later acute challenge, cf. the excluded Daphnia magna copper precedent)

title: Cumulative effects of successive marine heatwaves impair physiological resilience in the clam Ruditapes philippinarum.
reason: Ruditapes philippinarum given four successive simulated heatwaves (+1.5 and +5 C) with recuperation periods, then a later Vibrio tapetis challenge showing a carry-over effect of thermal history (near-total mortality); all four criteria hold, priming stressor is temperature

title: Addressing a flat-out problem: environmental DNA (eDNA) exposes silent infestations of Acropora-eating flatworms (Prosthiostomum acroporae) in coral aquaculture
reason: Methods-only eDNA/ddPCR assay development for detecting Acropora-eating flatworms in coral aquaculture; no priming exposure and no later-life outcome (criteria 2-4 fail; also an Authorea preprint)

title: Heat exposure improves acute copper tolerance in the intertidal copepod Tigriopus californicus.
reason: Intertidal copepod (Tigriopus californicus) given a sublethal heat exposure before acute copper toxicity testing (and the reverse order), with cross-protection measured; all four criteria hold. Cross-stressor priming-then-challenge design, in line with the Tigriopus and copepod precedents.

title: Early-Life Exposure to Warming Enhances Sea Urchin Heatwave Tolerance but Fails under Extreme Stress
reason: Echinoderm (Paracentrotus lividus) natural-history developmental warming contrast (power-plant thermal outfall vs naive population) followed by simulated category I and IV marine heatwave challenges; meets criteria 1-4 but is a bioRxiv preprint, so held until a peer-reviewed version appears

title: Heat priming protects oyster gills from subsequent lethal heat stress: Histopathology and apoptosis evidence in Crassostrea angulata.
reason: Crassostrea angulata sublethal heat priming followed by a lethal heat challenge, with gill histopathology and TUNEL apoptosis compared against lethal-only, sublethal-only and control groups; meets all four criteria (cf. Georgoulis_2021 heat hardening).

title: Assisted evolution of corals and their symbionts enhances recruit heat tolerance but with complex outcomes.
reason: Selective breeding of heat-tolerant broodstock plus inoculation with culture-evolved symbionts; no sublethal priming exposure applied to the coral host before the 32 C challenge (fails criterion 2), as in the selective-breeding and heat-evolved-symbiont precedents

title: The Benefit of Maternal Care and Infanticide by Males as Reproductive Strategies in a Caprellid Amphipod.
reason: Marine crustacean (caprellid amphipod) behavioural ecology study of maternal care and male infanticide; no sublethal priming exposure followed by a later-life or offspring assessment (fails criteria 2 and 3)

title: Unstable mitochondrial heteroplasmy in Mytilus edulis primary cell cultures.
reason: Primary cell culture study of mitochondrial heteroplasmy in Mytilus edulis (cell-culture-only, fails criterion 1); no sublethal priming exposure and no later-life or offspring outcome (criteria 2-3)

title: Evaluation of physiological and molecular tools to assess ovarian stages in the black tiger prawn (Penaeus monodon)
reason: Crustacean (Penaeus monodon) methods/staging study evaluating ovarian maturation markers in eyestalk-ablated broodstock; no sublethal priming exposure followed by a later assessment (fails criteria 2 and 3)

title: Comparative effects of sous vide, boiling, and frying on Antarctic krill proteins: links between oxidation, structural changes, in vitro digestibility, and peptidomic profiles.
reason: Food-science study of cooking effects on harvested krill muscle protein; no living animal conditioned, no sublethal priming exposure and no later-life outcome (fails criteria 2 and 3)

title: Genomic selection improves survival time under high ammonia nitrogen stress in Litopenaeus vannamei.
reason: Genomic selection / selective breeding for ammonia tolerance in Litopenaeus vannamei; no deliberate sublethal priming exposure followed by a later assessment (fails criterion 2) - the progeny contrast is genetic (GEBV groups), not conditioning

title: Low-Dose H2O2 Priming Improves Performance Under Simulated Marine Heatwave Conditions in a Coastal Bivalve.
reason: Ruditapes philippinarum primed with low-dose H2O2, thermal, or combined treatments then challenged with a simulated marine heatwave (plus months-long field follow-up); all four criteria hold, and the thermal-priming arm and heatwave challenge place it in the bivalve temperature cluster (cf. Martino_2026)

title: Parental CO₂-vent history does not improve larval performance of the sea urchin Arbacia lixula under copper and acidification
reason: Arbacia lixula parents from a natural CO2 vent vs ambient site (natural-history provenance contrast, criterion 2) with offspring reared in a crossed pH x copper design (criterion 3); would qualify like Kozal_2024, but it is a Research Square preprint - held until a peer-reviewed version appears

title: Embryonic hormetic priming modulates later-life thermal tolerance
reason: Pinctada margaritifera embryonic thermal priming (32 C) then 4 months common garden and 34 C spat challenge meets all four criteria, but it is an Authorea preprint (appears to be the preprint of the included Lugue_2026 study) - hold until the peer-reviewed version is confirmed and avoid double-counting

title: Thermal stress differentially regulates eicosanoid and fatty acid metabolism in gills of the blue mussel (Mytilus edulis).
reason: Bivalve and temperature, but the design compares a single acute heat shock with one week of repeated daily heat cycles, and lipid mediators are measured at the end of each exposure; there is no priming phase followed by a later challenge or post-conditioning assessment (fails criteria 2 and 3)

title: Species-level differences in molecular responses to a thermally variable stress-hardening treatment for Caribbean corals
reason: Authorea preprint of a diel-variable thermal stress-hardening treatment on A. cervicornis and P. clivosa (molecular companion to DeMerlis_2025); abstract reports expression during/after the hardening treatment but leaves open whether a later heat challenge was assessed (criterion 3 unclear) - hold until a peer-reviewed version appears, then check for folding into the DeMerlis_2025 row

title: Global warming and biological adaptation: Thermal priming buffers the impact of heatwaves on the reproductive health of the Mediterranean mussel Mytilus galloprovincialis.
reason: Mytilus galloprovincialis sublethal heat priming (28, 30 or 32 C for 2 h), 24 h recovery at 17 C, then 36 C heat-shock challenge compared with a directly shocked group; gonad histology and metabolomic outcomes measured after the challenge. All four criteria hold, matching the Georgoulis_2021 heat-hardening precedent.

title: Metabolic consequences of naturally occurring mitochondrial heteroplasmy in bivalves.
reason: Bivalve (Mytilus edulis, Ruditapes philippinarum) but a descriptive study of natural mitochondrial heteroplasmy and bioenergetics; no sublethal priming exposure and no later-life or offspring assessment (fails criteria 2 and 3)

title: Selective conservation of symbiont cell-surface glycans across generations in a vertically transmitting coral
reason: No priming exposure (criterion 2): descriptive parent-egg comparison of symbiont glycan profiles in Montipora capitata with no sublethal pre-exposure or later challenge; preprint status moot since it fails on merits

title: Food ration affects mRNA processing, translation, proteostasis and cytoskeletal responses during heat shock in Mytilus californianus.
reason: Mytilus californianus acclimated to low (20 C) vs high (30 C) daily aerial temperature crossed with food ration, then given a later acute 6 h 33 C aerial heat shock with 1 h and 25 h recovery; thermal conditioning followed by a later challenge satisfies criteria 2 and 3 (cf. Georgoulis_2021, Wang_2023)

title: Antagonistic effects of hypersalinity on heat tolerance in a copepod emerge from nonadditive protein abundance changes.
reason: Marine copepod (Tigriopus californicus) under hypersalinity x heat, but the abstract frames the design as simultaneous multistressor exposure; the 'chronic' salinity arm may be a salinity acclimation before an acute heat-tolerance assay (cross-tolerance priming) or may be concurrent. Full text is needed to settle criteria 2-3.

title: Genomic and GWAS-Based Insights into Antimicrobial Resistance in Shewanella algae Isolated from Penaeus monodon.
reason: Bacterial genomics/antimicrobial-resistance study of a Shewanella algae isolate cultured apart from the shrimp host; no priming exposure applied to a marine invertebrate and no later-life outcome (fails criteria 1-3)

title: [Association of maternal dietary intake, folic acid supplementation and offspring betaine-homocysteine methyltransferase (BHMT) and BHMT2 gene polymorphisms with congenital heart disease].
reason: Human case-control study of maternal diet and offspring congenital heart disease - not a marine invertebrate (fails inclusion criterion 1)

title: Gene body methylation suppresses intragenic transcription and permits epigenetic inheritance in a cnidarian.
reason: Cnidarian (Nematostella) mechanistic study of DNA methylation loss (genetic/methylation depletion) and its inheritance; no sublethal environmental priming exposure (fails criterion 2)

title: Selection of Vibrio parahaemolyticus isolates as potential vaccine candidates in Litopenaeus vannamei
reason: Penaeus/Litopenaeus vannamei vaccinated with inactivated VpAHPND isolates then challenged with live VpAHPND, with post-vaccination immune responses and survival measured (homologous vs heterologous protection); meets all four criteria, matching BermeoCapunong_2026 and Lin_2013 precedents

title: Estimation of genetic parameters for growth and shell color traits in the tetraploid 'Haida No. 3' line of Pacific oysters (Magallana gigas) in China.
reason: Bivalve quantitative-genetics study (heritability of growth and shell colour in tetraploid selected families); selective breeding with no sublethal priming exposure or later challenge - fails criterion 2

title: Bounded ecological memory in coral reefs: divergent demographic pathways under recurrent heatwaves and collapse under extreme thermal stress
reason: Colony-level field bleaching surveys and density analysis across Florida Reef Tract heatwaves; no controlled priming dose and no challenge applied to identified conditioned vs naive individuals (criterion 2), as with the repeated-thermal-stress field monitoring precedent. Preprint, but excluded on merits so no hold. NOTE FOR CURATOR: reports reduced bleaching after prior exposure that broke down under the 2023 MHW.

title: Genetic Diversity of Sexually Propagated Corals Is Maintained From the Aquarium to the Reef.
reason: Coral aquaculture population-genetics study tracking heterozygosity and parentage from aquarium to reef; no sublethal priming exposure applied before a later assessment (fails criterion 2).

title: A Bistable UV-Sensitive Opsin from a Reef Building Coral Showing a Switchable and Tunable Regulation of Gs-Signaling by Different Wavelengths of Light.
reason: Coral opsin biochemistry/optogenetics characterised in mammalian cultured cells; no priming exposure and no later-life outcome (fails criteria 1-3)

title: Multigenerational effects of polylactic acid microplastics on the microbiota of the sentinel copepod Eurytemora affinis.
reason: Estuarine copepod exposed to PLA microplastics over F0-F3 with a clean decontamination generation (F4) assessed for microbiota recovery; meets all four criteria, analogous to Zhao_2024 Tigriopus recovery-generation design (criterion 3 satisfied by post-exposure F4 assessment)

title: Peculiar stimulatory action of high-energy chemicals: Fifty years of explosive-induced hormesis evidence.
reason: Review synthesising five decades of explosive-induced hormesis across many taxa, not a primary empirical study (fails inclusion criterion 4); no priming-then-later-assessment design in marine invertebrates

title: Multigenerational machine learning-based genomic prediction for dermo resistance in eastern oyster Crassostrea virginica
reason: Genomic selection / machine-learning prediction of dermo resistance in Crassostrea virginica; selective breeding, not a priming exposure (fails criterion 2). Exclusion stands regardless of preprint status, so preprint_hold does not apply

title: Occurrence of Human Enteric Viruses in Retail Mussels Marketed in Burgos, Spain.
reason: Food-safety surveillance of enteric viruses (RT-qPCR) in retail Mytilus galloprovincialis; no deliberate priming exposure and no later challenge or later-life outcome (fails criteria 2 and 3)

title: Coral larval proteomics at onset of metamorphosis highlights innate immunity maturation in parallel to neuro-sensing and skeletal development.
reason: Descriptive developmental proteomics of Pocillopora acuta planula vs settler stages; 'maternal carry-over' refers to colony-of-origin variability, with no deliberate sublethal priming exposure and no later challenge (fails criteria 2 and 3)

title: Selective conservation of symbiont cell-surface glycans across generations in a vertically transmitting coral.
reason: No priming exposure (criterion 2): descriptive comparison of symbiont cell-surface glycans between Montipora capitata parents and eggs under vertical transmission; no sublethal pre-exposure and no later challenge or conditioned offspring outcome

title: Enhanced survival and lower growth in assisted gene flow corals during a marine heatwave driven by local adaptation
reason: Assisted gene flow / selective breeding across thermally distinct reefs; parental provenance is genetic, not an applied sublethal priming exposure (fails criterion 2); also a preprint

title: The toxicity of petroleum pollutants on marine zooplankton: Multiscale effects from individuals to populations.
reason: Review article, not a primary empirical study (fails inclusion criterion 4); petroleum pollutant effects on copepods/zooplankton

title: Probiotic and postbiotic treatment improves coral health and promotes specific metabolic and microbiome changes in situ during a heatwave.
reason: Probiotic/postbiotic microbial therapy applied concurrently during a natural heatwave, not a sublethal priming exposure followed by a later challenge (fails criterion 2; probiotics do not count by themselves)

title: Food-dependent activation of one-carbon metabolism during heat shock in Mytilus californianus.
reason: Bivalve (Mytilus californianus) acclimated to high (30 C) vs low (20 C) aerial low-tide temperatures, crossed with food ration, then given an acute 6 h 33 C aerial heat shock with 1 h and 25 h recovery; this preconditioning-then-challenge design meets criteria 2 and 3, consistent with Georgoulis_2021 and Bay_2015.

title: Proximity and current alignment drive fertilisation success in a broadcast-spawning coral (Acropora cf. hyacinthus).
reason: Coral fertilisation-ecology study manipulating colony spacing and current alignment; no sublethal priming exposure and no later-life or offspring challenge (fails criteria 2 and 3)

title: Distinct molecular mechanisms shape thermal tolerance and its plasticity in a splash pool copepod
reason: Tigriopus californicus (marine copepod) given a prior sub-lethal heat exposure before a later high-temperature survival assay across five populations; meets criteria 1-4 but is a bioRxiv preprint, so held until a peer-reviewed version appears

title: Recognition diversity and effector mechanisms of immunoglobulin superfamily proteins in invertebrates.
reason: Review article on invertebrate IgSF proteins and immune priming, not a primary empirical study (fails inclusion criterion 4)

title: Differential mercury tolerance in a planktonic copepod under different climate scenarios: A multigeneration perspective.
reason: Marine copepod (Pseudodiaptomus annandalei) multigenerational F1-F4 design in which ancestral vs offspring vs persistent acidification+warming exposure modulates later Hg toxicity, so ancestral AW is a priming exposure assessed in descendants; all four criteria hold (cf. Zhao_2024 Tigriopus, Thor_2015).

title: A bistable UV-sensitive opsin from a reef building coral showing a switchable and tunable regulation of Gs-signaling by different wavelengths of light
reason: Coral opsin characterisation in mammalian cultured cells (cell-culture-only, criterion 1); no sublethal priming exposure or later assessment (criteria 2-3). Preprint, but exclusion takes precedence over hold

title: Contrasting patterns of seascape genetics in Acropora cf. tenuis and their symbiotic algae
reason: Seascape/population genetics survey of Acropora cf. tenuis and Cladocopium; no sublethal priming exposure and no later challenge (fails criteria 2 and 3), so excluded outright rather than held as a preprint

title: Introgression of thermal tolerance alleles drives adaptation despite risk of mitonuclear conflict.
reason: Hybridisation plus ten generations of experimental selection for thermal tolerance in Tigriopus californicus (genetic selection/introgression), not a sublethal priming exposure followed by a later assessment - fails criterion 2

title: Acclimatization potential in stress tolerant Caribbean corals - outcomes of a 5 year cross-shelf reciprocal transplant experiment
reason: bioRxiv preprint. Five-year nearshore/offshore reciprocal transplant of P. strigosa and S. siderea, followed by bleaching assessment during the natural 2024 marine heatwave. This resembles Palumbi_2014 and Klepac_2020 (transplant into a distinct environment, then heat stress) more than the excluded Siderastrea transplant, which had no later thermal challenge. Criterion 2 is a scope call needing the full text; held as a preprint until a peer-reviewed version appears.

title: Food Ration Affects mRNA Processing, Translation, Proteostasis, and Cytoskeletal Responses During Heat Shock in Mytilus californianus
reason: Bivalve (Mytilus californianus) acclimated to high vs low aerial temperature (crossed with food ration) and then given a later acute 6 h 33 C heat shock with proteomic recovery assessment, so criteria 1-4 hold. The conditioning-then-challenge design resembles Georgoulis_2021, but the paper is a bioRxiv preprint and is held until a peer-reviewed version appears.

title: The risk of thiamine deficiency in common eider ducklings increases when females consume large prey.
reason: Bird (common eider) modelling study - fails inclusion criterion 1 (mussels are only the measured prey, not the conditioned organism); also a model with no priming exposure (criteria 2 and 4)

title: Acclimatization modulates energy metabolism in an aquatic amphipod under exposure to ciprofloxacin and thiacloprid.
reason: Freshwater amphipod (Gammarus fossarum) - fails the marine/estuarine inclusion criterion 1; 'acclimatization' is laboratory holding time before a single 21 d pollutant exposure, not a sublethal priming exposure

title: Thermal pre-treatment of algal symbiont species differentially affects coral development
reason: Thermal pre-treatment was applied to cultured algal symbionts, not to the coral host; larvae only received the pre-exposed algae, so priming was not applied to the invertebrate (criterion 2). Also a bioRxiv preprint, but the exclusion takes precedence over a preprint hold.

title: Global macroecological patterns of larval size in decapods are governed by temperature and dissolved oxygen.
reason: Comparative macroecological/phylogenetic analysis of decapod larval size across species; no deliberate sublethal priming exposure (criterion 2), no later-life or offspring challenge (criterion 3), and not a primary conditioning experiment (criterion 4)

title: An Integrated Oceanographic and Physiological Framework for Identifying Climate Refugia for Marine Invertebrates
reason: Modelling/mapping framework for thermal refugia of green abalone from satellite SST and fisheries CPUE; no deliberate priming exposure or later challenge on animals, and not a primary conditioning experiment (fails criteria 2-4)

title: An Integrated Oceanographic and Physiological Framework for Identifying Climate Refugia for Marine Invertebrates.
reason: Spatial modelling framework mapping thermal refugia for green abalone from satellite SST and fisheries CPUE; no deliberate priming exposure or later challenge on animals and not a primary conditioning experiment (fails criteria 2 and 4)

title: Rapid RPA-CRISPR/Cas12a detection of Vibrio coralliilyticus for coral aquaculture disease surveillance
reason: Diagnostic assay development for Vibrio coralliilyticus in bacterial DNA and tank water; a methods-only paper with no priming exposure applied to corals and no later outcome (fails criteria 2-4). It is a preprint, but preprint_hold applies only to papers that would otherwise be include or needs_full_text.

title: Melanin-concentrating hormone inhibits PVN oxytocin neurons through a barium-sensitive inwardly rectifying potassium channels and MCH-neuron ablation alters pup-directed aggression
reason: Rodent neuroendocrine study (MCH/oxytocin neurons, pup-directed aggression) - not a marine invertebrate, fails inclusion criterion 1; no priming exposure; preprint status moot since it would be excluded anyway

title: Early-life environmental conditions shape demographic responses to climate change in male Antarctic fur seals
reason: Marine mammal (Antarctic fur seal), not a marine invertebrate - fails inclusion criterion 1; also observational natal-environment carry-over with no deliberate priming exposure, and a bioRxiv preprint

title: Ectomycorrhizal Symbiosis as a Bio-Enhancement Strategy for Transplantation of Somatic Embryo-Derived Pinus elliottii.
